about.title: About AMVerge
about.subtitle: AMVerge makes scene selection easier. It splits an episode into every scene, so you can skim through it much faster and miss less scenes than you would in a video editor.

what.title: What is AMVerge?
what.p1: A clip cutter for anime editors. Give it an episode and it finds every shot change, then lays the whole thing out as a grid you can skim.
what.p2: Click the scenes you want and it pulls them out of the source file without re-encoding, so the clips keep the quality of the original. They land in a folder ready to drag into After Effects, Premiere, or Resolve.
what.p3: It doesn't edit anything for you or decide which scenes are good. It just takes out the part where you scrub through an episode hunting for the four seconds you remembered.

workflow.title: Fast Workflow
workflow.import: Import: Drag & drop your video files (MP4, MKV, WebM, etc.).
workflow.select: Select: Skim the grid and select the scenes you need. Use Shift + Click for ranges or Ctrl + Click for individual clips.
workflow.export: Merge & Export: Pick an export profile (or enable Merge Clips to join sequences) and hit Export Now.

resources.title: Resources
resources.subtitle: Free, noteworthy tools made by the AMV community

resyncbot.tagline: Automatically resync edits in seconds with your friends
resyncbot.details: Used in 300+ servers with nearly 200,000 people, this is a discord bot made by the AMVerge creator that resyncs edits automatically in seconds. Using BPM & audio waveform analysis, you can automatically resync your edit to a desired one or roll a random one that would fit.
resyncbot.devNote: This was my first project, and probably the most fun one I've made, to my surprise it's still being used many times a day, and as a result I'll be maintaining this for as long as I can.

sammieRoto.details: Co-created by the developer of AMVerge's Scene Scout feature, this is a free, open source AI masking tool featuring object detection + removal, and an exclusive AI model trained on anime. So good that it even captures hair strands flawlessly (Adobe, take notes..)
sammieRoto.devNote: Quite literally the best rotobrush tool I have used, their anime model blew my mind. Would highly recommend this if you haven't tried it already.

animeclips.details: With over 450,000+ clips, this is the largest library and resource for high quality anime clips.
animeclips.devNote: This is a resource I've used for a while now if I can't find a download for an anime I'm looking to edit, and a website trusted by thousands of editors today. Highly recommend!

hyetta.details: A place to host editing contests, catered towards hour contests (HCs). It has its own judging sheet with an scorer that automates things like score sums and late penalties, is super intuitive, and gives you one easy place to hold all of an event's entries.
hyetta.devNote: This platform handles all the annoying parts of hosting an HC for you, aside from the anime selection / limitations.
